items.answer: A platform is the combination of hardware and an operating system.

An authoring tool is a tool that lets a developer create software or content by accessing underlying system functionalities, with options for loading, feature-setting, and logic-setting; for augmented reality, it can be standalone or an existing tool extended by a plugin.

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.
A marker is a real-world object or image placed in the environment that a system detects to identify its position or track a user's motion and to place digital content at that position.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Three-dimensional registration is the anchoring of virtual content in augmented reality at a suitable place in the real world so that it appears to be part of the physical environment and mixes seamlessly with real-world objects.

questions.question: Which three kinds of criterion are used to classify augmented reality software tools?
options: Developer skill, application size, and rendering technique
Developer skill, target platform, and display technology
Developer skill, target platform, and tracking technology
Programming language, target platform, and input method
questions.explanation: AR software tools can be categorized by the developer's skill level, the application platform they target, or the tracking technology they use. Display technology, input method, application size, and rendering technique are not the given classification criteria.

questions.question: Which category of augmented reality software requires the strongest programming or coding ability?
questions.explanation: Low-level software libraries or frameworks require the strongest programming or coding ability and understanding of how to call their functions. The other categories require less programming, a different tool skill, or no programming at all.

questions.question: Which category of augmented reality software can be used without any programming ability?
questions.explanation: Standalone AR authoring tools assume no programming ability. By contrast, low-level tools require strong programming, rapid prototyping tools require some programming, and plugins require skill with the original developer tool.

data.text: AR software tools can be sorted by developer skill, target application platform, or tracking technology. A skill-based classification places them in four categories, moving from low-level libraries and rapid-prototyping tools to plugins and standalone authoring tools. The required skill falls as the categories move from coding-heavy tools toward tools that need no programming knowledge.
points: AR software tools can be categorized by developer skill, target application platform, or tracking technology.
The four skill-based AR software categories are low-level libraries, rapid prototyping tools, plugins, and standalone authoring tools.
AR skill requirements fall from coding and library use, to some coding or prototyping, to developer-tool skill, to no programming.

questions.question: Which characteristic makes low-level AR libraries and frameworks the most skill-demanding software category?
options: They hide tracking behind a ready-made authoring tool
They limit development to a single platform and tracker
They provide finished interaction and realistic graphics
They give access to core tracking and display functions
questions.explanation: Low-level AR software gives developers direct access to the core tracking and display functionality needed to build an AR application, so they must manage those functions directly. The other options describe higher-level or restrictive tools rather than the low-level category.

questions.question: Why is a complete realistic AR application difficult to build with ARToolKit alone?
options: It provides interaction but not tracking or display
It provides natural-feature tracking but not marker tracking or display
It provides realistic rendering but not tracking or interaction
It provides tracking but not interaction or realistic rendering
questions.explanation: ARToolKit is primarily a tracking-support library, and its rendering is low-level and primitive, so interaction and complex realistic graphics must be added separately. Options that credit ARToolKit with interaction or realistic rendering reverse its actual role.

questions.question: When ARToolKit is paired with a scene-graph library, which task does the scene-graph library mainly perform?
questions.explanation: The scene-graph library handles low-level rendering of the virtual content, while ARToolKit handles tracking and 3D registration. Marker tracking and sensor reading belong to the tracking side.

questions.question: Which tracking capability is available in ARToolKit's commercial version but not in its open-source version?
options: GPS-based tracking for outdoor mobile use
Natural-feature tracking on an arbitrary image
questions.explanation: The commercial ARToolKit version adds computer-vision tracking of natural features on an arbitrary image, while the open-source version is marker-based. GPS and phone-motion tracking are not the added capability of the commercial version.

data.text: Low-level AR software gives developers direct access to core tracking and display, but ARToolKit is mainly a tracking-support library with primitive rendering and little interaction support. Scene graph libraries such as Open Scene Graph and Vulkan Scene Graph manage rendering and interaction, so combining them with ARToolKit allows tracking and rendered virtual content to work together in AR frameworks and mobile tools.
points: Low-level AR libraries and frameworks expose core tracking and display functionality, so they demand the most developer skill.
ARToolKit is a widely used C library that mainly provides tracking, marker-based openly and natural-feature commercially.
ARToolKit and many tracking-focused toolkits provide primitive rendering and no interaction support, making complete realistic AR apps difficult and time-consuming.
Scene graphs such as OSG or VSG are C++ OpenGL libraries that manage complex 3D rendering and interaction.
Combining ARToolKit tracking with OSG or VSG rendering supports AR scenes, including example frameworks and mobile frameworks.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of rapid prototyping and development tools in augmented-reality projects?
options: To replace a low-level library for clients before major development
To show a simple visualization for end users before major development
To provide maximum flexibility for developers before major development
To remove camera tracking for clients before major development
questions.explanation: Rapid prototyping and development tools let an AR idea be visualized with simple means and shown to end users or clients before major development, so an unsuitable idea does not need further coding. They are not primarily for low-level flexibility, replacing libraries, or removing camera tracking.

questions.question: Why can implementing an augmented-reality application directly with low-level AR libraries be time-consuming?
options: Because it requires significant programming skill
Because it requires markerless tracking support
Because it requires a Flash-enabled web browser
Because it requires a Flash AR Manager framework
questions.explanation: Low-level AR libraries give maximum flexibility, but using them requires knowing the library or framework and writing programs, so implementation takes time and significant programming skill. Flash-based tools or markerless tracking are not requirements of low-level AR libraries in general.

questions.question: What allows FLAR Toolkit to let a user develop an augmented-reality experience with minimal effort?
options: Its marker tracking and content overlay are possible with a few lines of code
Its markerless tracking and content placement are possible with a few lines of code
Its library combination and graphics rendering are possible with a few lines of code
Its low-level coding and manual rendering are possible with a few lines of code
questions.explanation: FLAR Toolkit lets a user activate a camera, track AR markers, and overlay virtual content using only a few lines of code, so little programming is needed. Combining libraries is the role of FLAR Manager, and FLAR Toolkit is marker-based rather than markerless.

questions.question: What is Flash AR Manager designed to combine AR tracking and graphics libraries for?
options: For prototyping rather than full-fledged development
For low-level library authoring rather than full-fledged development
For non-Flash prototyping rather than full-fledged development
For deployment rather than full-fledged development
questions.explanation: Flash AR Manager is a framework that combines AR tracking libraries with 3D graphics libraries, and such combinations are used primarily for prototyping rather than full-fledged development. It is not aimed at deployment, low-level library authoring, or non-Flash workflows.

data.text: Low-level AR libraries are contrasted with rapid prototyping tools, showing why prototyping is useful before major development. Flash-based prototyping uses Adobe Flash with AR plugins to create desktop or mobile AR experiences. FLAR Toolkit makes browser-based marker tracking and 3D overlay simple, while Flash AR Manager combines tracking libraries with 3D graphics libraries mainly for prototypes.
points: Low-level AR libraries offer maximum flexibility but require substantial programming and are time-consuming.
Rapid prototyping tools visualize an AR idea for users or clients before major development.
Adobe Flash can be used with AR plugins to prototype desktop and mobile AR experiences.
FLAR Toolkit runs Flash AR in a browser, with few lines of code tracking markers and overlaying 3D content.
Flash AR Manager combines AR tracking libraries with 3D graphics libraries, mainly for prototyping rather than full development.

items.reason: AR Toolkit, OSG Art, and StudiersTube are low-level AR software libraries or frameworks, while OpenFrameworks is a rapid prototyping tool.
Vuforia, MetaIO Unity Plugin, and Dart are plugins for existing developer tools, while MetaIO Creator is a standalone AR authoring tool.
BuildAR, Wikitude, and MetaIO Creator are standalone AR authoring tools, while FLAR Manager is a rapid prototyping tool.

questions.question: Why does a skill-based classification place low-level augmented reality software libraries or frameworks at the highest programming-skill end and standalone augmented reality authoring tools at the no-programming end?
questions.reference_answer: The skill-based hierarchy orders tools by decreasing programming skill. Low-level libraries or frameworks sit highest because they require strong programming, require knowing how to call library functions, and give access to core tracking and display functionality. Standalone authoring tools sit lowest because they assume no programming ability and can be used without any knowledge.

questions.question: How does combining ARToolKit with a scene graph library make it easier to build a complete realistic augmented reality application than using ARToolKit alone?
questions.reference_answer: ARToolKit alone provides only primitive OpenGL-based rendering and no built-in interaction support, so interaction must be written from scratch and a complete realistic application is difficult. A framework can combine tracking-focused libraries with libraries that provide interaction and realistic graphics. With a scene graph library, low-level object rendering is handled while ARToolKit remains responsible for tracking, letting the developer focus on interaction.

questions.question: Why might a developer choose a Flash-based rapid prototyping tool to test an augmented reality idea before major development?
questions.reference_answer: Rapid prototyping tools let an augmented reality idea be visualized with simple means and shown to end users or clients, so an unsuitable idea does not require further coding. Flash-based tools may be chosen because they have greater market penetration, and Adobe Flash can be used with augmented reality plugins to prototype desktop and mobile experiences.

questions.question: How does the desktop-versus-mobile categorization of augmented reality software tools correspond to the deployment meaning of a platform as operating system plus hardware?
questions.reference_answer: In augmented reality software categorization, the target application platform can be a desktop or a mobile augmented reality application. In deployment, a platform means the operating system plus hardware, with Windows or Mac OS representing desktop platforms and Android or iOS representing mobile platforms, so the categories name the target operating-system and hardware environment.
